messages:
oncall-bot: ALERT: GPU_POOL_SATURATION detected in us-east-1/hotpath-pool — queue length=1,240 (rising), 95p latency=32.4s, 429 spike 00:02:15. Severity=P2. Paging oncall.
Anna (oncall): seen it. I'm looking at pool metrics now. queue retention shows lots of long-running requests.
Anna (oncall): @Chris can you grab autoscaler logs? I suspect we hit max_nodes and autoscale didn't kick in.
Chris (sre): on it. pulling autoscaler events... `kubectl -n infra logs deploy/autoscaler --since=30m` — seeing repeated "scale-reached-max" and "scale-back-cooldown" messages.
Chris (sre): autoscaler config shows max_nodes=64 for hotpath; current nodes=64. attempts to add blocked by limit.
Maria (eng-runtime): I also see a huge number of 429s at the gateway tier policy layer. Token-bucket drop rate up 18x. Lots of requests get a 429 with header X-Rate-Limit: token_bucket.
Kevin (infra): timeline: deploy-bot applied a config change ~13m ago: rate-tier policy update (commit: git@repo:infra/tier-policies@b9c1f). Could be related.
deploy-bot: Deployed tier-policies.yaml to prod (us-east-1) at 1901239060 by maria. Link: https://git.internal/infra/commit/b9c1f
Anna (oncall): @Maria can you confirm what changed in the commit? short diff pls.
Maria (eng-runtime): small change: adjusted token_bucket refill_rate for "standard" tier to 1. But I think units are ms in the new parser. The intended value was 1 token/s but the runtime interprets as tokens/ms — this makes effective refill 1000x too fast OR too slow? checking.
Chris (sre): looking at counters. tokens_consumed/sec jumped then dropped to zero; explanation: bucket drained instantly because refill_rate was treated as tokens/ms and set to 1 -> actually too high? hmm.
Maria (eng-runtime): hold on: new parser uses refill_rate as "tokens_per_second" but the YAML author used an old comment. Wait other way: our stack expects "tokens_per_ms" for legacy reasons. The commit mistakenly changed unit comment and people wrote 1 meaning 1 token/ms which is 1000 tokens/s — that would increase capacity not reduce it. Not matching 429 spike.
Kevin (infra): alternative: the patch also set burst_size to 0 for non-enterprise tiers as an emergency limit. I see that in the diff: `burst_size: 0` for standard tier. That would cause instant throttles during spikes.
Maria (eng-runtime): yep found it. The diff:
```
standard:
  token_bucket:
    size: 1000
    refill_rate: 1
    burst_size: 0
```
Old value was burst_size: 100. I think burst_size=0 is the culprit — removes cushion so short surges get 429.
Jess (customer-success): I'm getting DMs from a customer about failing requests. Which customers impacted? any high-value ones?
Chris (sre): using logs: top impacted API keys: acct-3112, acct-4759, acct-8891. All standard tier. No enterprise-tier keys hit 429s yet.
Anna (oncall): mitigation plan step 1: restore burst_size to previous value for standard tier to stop immediate throttles. Step 2: increase hotpath pool max_nodes to allow scale while we stabilize. Step 3: backfill queue and enable temporary routing to coldpath for large payloads.
Kevin (infra): I can bump autoscaler max_nodes now. running:
```
kubectl -n infra set env deploy/autoscaler MAX_NODES=160
kubectl -n infra rollout restart deploy/autoscaler
```
Kevin (infra): done — autoscaler env updated, restart triggered. monitor events.
Chris (sre): applying tier fix now. editing tier-policies in prod: revert burst_size to 100 for standard tier and apply.
Chris (sre): `rictl config apply --file tier-policies.yaml --target=us-east-1` -> accepted.
deploy-bot: Config apply started at 1901240120: tier-policies.yaml -> us-east-1
deploy-bot: Config apply succeeded at 1901240145
Maria (eng-runtime): after config revert, I'm seeing token-bucket rejects drop sharply. 429 rate down 80% in 2m.
Anna (oncall): good. Chris, did autoscaler pick up new nodes?
Chris (sre): nodes scaling: +28 added over last 6m. current nodes=92. queue length dropping: 1,240 -> 420.
Maria (eng-runtime): additionally, I'll push a small parser validation to prevent burst_size=0 for standard tier in future. creating PR.
Anna (oncall): customer comms: @Jess can you post a short status to affected customers saying we had rate-tier misconfig, mitigation applied, and we're monitoring? include ETA ~30m.
Jess (customer-success): posting now. DMing top impacted accounts and opening support tickets.
Jess (customer-success): message sent to acct-3112 and acct-4759. will escalate if they report continued errors.
Chris (sre): discovered secondary issue: a separate autoscale cooldown window was set to 10m in the same config change (earlier deploy), which slowed scaling reaction. I'm temporarily lowering cooldown to 60s.
Chris (sre): `kubectl -n infra exec deploy/autoscaler -- /bin/sh -c 'update-config cooldown=60' && kubectl -n infra rollout restart deploy/autoscaler`
Chris (sre): cooldown lowered and rollout started.
Kevin (infra): note — we hit cloud provider quota for hotpath GPUs at 120 total in us-east-1; increased nodes succeeded because we used spare capacity from burst pool allocation. need follow-up with capacity planning.
Anna (oncall): on-call handoff: I'm going offline in ~15m. @Chris will take ownership after I drop. I'll leave a summary:
Anna (oncall): summary: cause = tier-policies change set burst_size=0 + cooldown increased -> combined to produce throttles and slow autoscale. Mitigations applied: reverted burst_size, raised autoscaler max_nodes, lowered cooldown, routed heavy jobs to coldpath. Monitoring shows recovery.
Chris (sre): acknowledged, taking oncall. watching dashboards.
Maria (eng-runtime): PR opened to add linter for tier-policies and a guard in deploy pipeline to reject burst_size=0 for standard. PR: https://git.internal/infra/pull/4321
Maria (eng-runtime): also adding an alert for sudden 429-rate spike with correlation to token-bucket changes.
Jess (customer-success): customers replied — some report transient errors cleared, one still seeing timeouts (acct-8891). triaging with eng.
Chris (sre): acct-8891 trace shows requests stuck in queue timeout (client timeout 60s). We need to increase queue timeout temporarily to let existing backlog finish.
Kevin (infra): bumped gateway timeout for queue route to 120s for hotpath via lb rule update.
Chris (sre): gateway timeout bumped. queue drain progress looks good: 420 -> 48 over 18m.
Anna (oncall): great work. leaving notes in incident tracker and will attach logs + command history.
Anna (oncall): final status at 1901243420: queue=28, 429-rate normalized, nodes=95, autoscaler healthy. I'll close the page in 30m unless new alerts.
oncall-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations applied, paging stopped. Please link postmortem when available.
Jess (customer-success): filing customer incident notes and sending a short follow-up to impacted customers summarizing root cause and remediation.
Chris (sre): I'll own the postmortem. tag me for follow-ups. adding timeline and config diffs to the doc.
Anna (oncall): thanks team. :thumbsup:
